findings: No new leak or cycle found in six independent native-capacity scheduling probes.
All choosing/guard/ref-increment operations are synchronous before physical acquire; same registry cannot change selection during that segment.

shard.owner is assigned after successful acquire and cleared inside try/finally before release. refs include owners and queued callers, so owner=None/locked=False during handoff does not bypass refusal.
Same-task shard reentry increments only refs: outer successful acquire retains task held.overflow and ownership until the whole nested body ends. A foreign task remains excluded across inner exit.

Cancellation before successful physical acquire decrements refs without creating task state; cancellation inside nested reentry unwinds inner refs then outer held count/owner and releases physical lock.

Any task already holding this registry refuses a foreign live overflow queue. A task holding overflow also refuses a live dedicated queue. Thus a new wait edge while holding locks can only be pure-dedicated; physical shard coarsening cannot close a cycle.

Pure-dedicated sharing callers use therapist-before-patient; multiple therapist IDs use sorted unique IDs in rekey, and multiple patient IDs in rotation are sorted. Other patient loops release each patient guard before the next. No same dedicated-key recursion found in production callers.
review_boundary: Generic same-key dedicated reentry and arbitrary caller inversions are not added promises; current consumers obey logical ordering. Cross-registry consumer order is reviewed separately: lifecycle precedes sharing/notes and collection locks; audit append fences are innermost and do not acquire lifecycle/sharing.
pending_scope: Entire changed locks module must be re-enumerated and replayed. No old locks kill/equivalence credit transfers automatically.
